title: Technical Lead, Power Systems Infrastructure
description:
Meta runs a massive hardware infrastructure. The computational problems are big and they keep changing. Your work will shape the power strategies for the compute and AI hardware going into our data centers. We are looking for an experienced power engineer to set the technical direction for power across our server infrastructure.The scope is the full power chain, from the data center interface to the die. Everything between the building's electrical infrastructure and the IT load, high-voltage DC distribution to the rack, AC/DC and DC/DC conversion in the rack, and DC/DC power delivery on the board. Point of load conversion and power delivery networks feed our accelerators and CPUs at hundreds of amps and sub millivolt tolerances. The multi-hundred-kilowatt AI rack is where they meet.This is a technical leadership role that owns the power roadmap. Internally, the role works with silicon, platform, thermal, data center design, and capacity teams to define where power architecture needs to go two to three generations out. Externally, it is Meta's technical voice with power vendors, ODMs, and the industry. That includes the Open Compute Project, where we have contributed our designs for over a decade.  
  
  

### **Technical Lead, Power Systems Infrastructure Responsibilities:**

* Own Meta's multi-generation rack and row power architecture strategy. This spans AC/DC and DC/DC in the rack and high-voltage DC delivery to the rack. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to adopt architectures across infrastructure
* Own the DC/DC power conversion architecture for accelerators and CPUs. Point of load topology, power delivery network design, vertical power delivery, telemetry and control. Drive it with silicon, package, and platform teams from silicon requirements through production
* Set the technical direction for power technology development and industry alignment. Supplier and ecosystem readiness has to match the hardware roadmap at scale. This applies to AC/DC and DC
